newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - UK equity traders wait for U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - UK equity traders wait for U.S. data.

text.p: UK equity options traders were not taking any chances and many decided not trade in case of being wrong-footed ahead of the U.S. employment report on Friday, dealers said.
"The figures have a habit of producing surprises and people have decided it wasn't worth taking any additional risk (in the options market)," one dealer said.
In stock options Reuters Holdings and British Petroleum attracted the larger deals whereas volatility trades were popular in the European style FTSE 100 index options.
Dealers believed the spike up in shares of news and information company Reuters prompted one trader to roll forward a long put position.
The deal was to sell 400 April 600 puts at 22p in a closing deal and to buy 400 July 550 puts at 16p in a new opening position.
By 1215 GMT, Reuters shares were up 11-1/2p to 588p.
On the bull tack, over in BP, one large deal was to buy 500 October 800 calls at 12p and in a separate deal, there was a seller of 250 July 650 puts at 19p.
The main volatility trades in FTSE were from traders expecting near-term market volatility to decrease and so they sold strangles which were hedged by FTSE futures.
In one such deal 250 April 4225 puts and calls in Euro-FTSE were sold for a net credit of 102p against June FTSE futures at 4251.
By 1215 GMT, spot FTSE was up 25.0 at 4239.6 while June futures were up 21 at 4258.
